intro: Four connected questions run through my work: what a model represents internally, when its reasoning can be trusted, how agents should coordinate and plan, and how these systems can support people making real decisions.

themes.title: Interpretability & Representations
themes.question: What do language models encode internally — and can we read or steer it?
themes.summary: Linear probing, activation steering, and intervention-based analysis of internal representations, including epistemic uncertainty and negation in biomedical language models.

themes.title: LLM Reasoning & Adaptive Computation
themes.question: When does extra computation, such as self-reflection, actually help a model reason?
themes.summary: Counterfactual evaluation of reasoning trajectories and learned signals for deciding when a model should reflect.

themes.title: Agentic & Multi-Agent Systems
themes.question: How should agents plan, coordinate, and stay safe under uncertainty and failure?
themes.summary: Planner-driven orchestration, dependency-aware execution, constrained control for autonomous agents, and resilient coordination under degraded communication.

themes.title: Trustworthy & Human-Centered AI
themes.question: How do we make AI systems reliable, grounded, and fair to the people relying on them?
themes.summary: Reliability and safety evaluation, source-grounded evidence retrieval, privacy-preserving language modeling, and studying bias in multi-agent synthesis of stakeholder perspectives.
